question: A specific geometric feature is revealed when we slice directly through a solid object. Which of the following best defines a cross section in geometry?
options: The total surface area of all the flat faces on a 3D object.
The total volume of material required to build a 3D object.
The 2D shape exposed when cutting straight through a 3D object.
The longest continuous straight edge of a polyhedron.

question: Consider a solid cylinder. We understand that 3D shapes can have more than one type of cross section depending on the cutting angle. Depending on which way you cut a cylinder, the cross section can be either a rectangle OR a ______.

A geometry student is tasked with matching various 2D cross sections back to their original 3D objects. The student finds a flat 2D rectangle. Which of the following 3D shapes could NOT possibly produce a rectangular cross section?
If the cross section of an unknown solid object is perfectly circular, which of the following shapes could the solid possibly be?
options: A cylinder, a sphere, or a cone

question: You are handed a flat 2D circle and asked to identify which 3D solid it originally came from. Why is it mathematically impossible to know for sure if it came from a sphere, a cylinder, or a cone just by examining the circular cross section?
options: Because cones only ever produce triangular cross sections.
Because cylinders only ever produce rectangular cross sections.
Because a circle cannot legally be a cross section.
Because many different 3D shapes can share the exact same 2D cross sections depending on how they are cut.
